Subject: Renewal planning — need pricing for expansion + credits

Hi Naomi,

Hope you had a good week. We're preparing our FY28 budget and want to lock a renewal discussion with Redwood. A few asks from Procurement and Engineering: 

- We expect to increase inference capacity ~2x over the next 6 months (more batch embeddings + chat).
- We'd like options for a 12–24 month term, with a mechanism to true-up monthly.
- Can you outline any bridge credits or onboarding credits you can offer if we sign earlier?
- Engineering requested an SLA carveout for p95 gen latency for a specific route (kept under 80ms) — is that possible or do we need a separate SLA addon?

Attached a usage extract for Q1 to help model comps. Would you be able to send a proposed pricing pathway and any optional add-ons (burst insurance, reserved capacity) by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Ava

Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lemos <ava.lemos@priorityenergy.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — need pricing for expansion + credits

Ava —

Thanks for the usage extract, that helps a lot. High-level proposal we can share now (I'll attach a worked example with numbers):

1) Term & Commit: 18-month staged commit by quarter (Q1: current baseline, Q2: +25%, Q3: +50% from baseline). If you want 12 or 24 months we can map the same staged cadence.

2) Price hold: We can hold current list rates for the first 6 months on the granted commit; after that, list rates follow our published catalog with a 3% annual cap.

3) Credits & Onboarding: One-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first 3 months' committed spend (applied as usage credits). Additionally, we can offer a bridge credit up to $60k if you sign before April 15 to cover migration spikes.

4) Burst insurance: optional +5% of committed spend monthly to enable a burst pool that auto-bills at a reduced overage rate. This is useful if you expect ephemeral surges (we'll reserve capacity and prioritize routing).

5) SLA carveouts: For the specific inference route, we can include a tailored SLA at a premium (negotiable). We can commit a p95 latency objective and provide financial credits for violations, but it requires a routing policy pinned to dedicated capacity or a guaranteed portion of dedicated instances.

Next steps: I've attached a pricing pathway workbook that models these options against the CSV you sent (redwood_pricing_pathway_v2.xlsx). Ben — would you please model a version that adds an incremental 30% commit and show the delta on credits vs list? Priyom — can you confirm whether the onboarding credit and bridge credit need legal review for any redlines?

I can join a call with Procurement and Engineering on Monday afternoon PT if that helps.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0198

Quick note from pricing ops after a first pass:

- Modeling the 30% uplift (baseline from the CSV) shows the onboarding credit and the April bridge credit materially reduce effective first-quarter unit cost; I'll attach two scenarios (with/without burst insurance).
- We have room to add a one-time additional 5% promotional discount on committed spend if the customer signs >= 30% uplift and agrees to an 18-month term. That will need Marissa's nod (it's outside standard discount matrix).
- The SLA carveout is doable if the customer accepts a dedicated slice for that route; ops needs the expected sustained throughput numbers to size it.

Marissa — can you approve the extra 5% on deal DEAL-9876 if Procurement signs an 18-month staged commit? If you prefer, we can make it conditional on a performance milestone after month 3.

Ben

Naomi/Ben,

Thanks for the quick proposal. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule exec approval: 

- Term preference: procurement will not approve > 12 months without a monthly true-up option and a cap on annual escalations. Can you add a clause for a monthly true-up with a +/- 15% window?
- Bridge credit timing: bridge credit is helpful, but we need it to be applied to usage (not professional services) and visible on our invoice line items.
- SLA: we need to see a written SLA addendum and the SLOs you measure against. If dedicated capacity is required, please include an estimate of the monthly charge for the dedicated slice.
- Compliance: attach your SOC 2 Type II report and data residency statements for our legal team.

I've attached our procurement checklist and a redlined template of terms we usually sign. Happy to do a 30-min call Tuesday PST to walk through.

Procurement
Priority Energy
